html:
The Vanyumé were a people of the Mojave River in the western Mojave Desert of southern California. They spoke a Takic language close to that of the Serrano, and are often counted as a branch of them.

They lived in small villages along the river, which runs mostly underground, and traded between the coast and the Colorado River, a route also used by the Mojave. Their other neighbours were the Kitanemuk and the Tongva. Spanish missions drew many of them away in the early 1800s, and by the late 1800s they had disappeared as a separate people. Little of their language was ever written down.
